name: Custom Small Stickers
seoTitle: Custom Small Stickers and Mini Stickers from 0.5 Inch
seoDescription: Custom small stickers from 0.5" to 2": mini logos, jar seals, tiny labels and sticker sheets printed sharp on vinyl or paper. Any shape, free proof.
tagline: Mini stickers from 0.5" to 2", cut clean and printed sharp enough to read at that size.
quickAnswer: Custom small stickers are printed stickers between 0.5" and 2" on their longest side: logo dots, jar and box seals, mini labels, planner stickers and tiny die cut shapes. They are printed on vinyl, BOPP, paper or kraft and supplied as singles, kiss cut sheets or rolls for makers, product brands and packaging lines. From $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production.
highlights: Material: vinyl, BOPP, paper or kraft

sections.h2: Half-inch seals, one-inch logos, two-inch labels
sections.html:
A 1" sticker is a different printing problem from a 6" one. Type that reads fine on a laptop sticker turns to mush at mini size, die cut tolerances that nobody notices on a big piece become half the sticker, and the backing has to be easy to peel with a fingernail. This page is where we deal with all of that. Its sibling, our custom large sticker range, covers the other end, 12" and up, where the problems are tiling, bubbles and whether the artwork has enough resolution. Small stickers are about legibility and handling.

We print minis for jar and tin seals, mini logo stickers slipped into orders, planner and journal sheets, product labels on lip balm and sample vials, price and SKU dots, phone and earbud case decorations, envelope seals and the stickers kids trade.

sections.h2: Small sticker sizes and what fits on each
sections.html:
Use this table to pick a size before you design, since the size decides how much the sticker can carry.

SizeWhat fitsTypical jobFormat
0.5" to 0.75"A single icon or letter, no textEnvelope seals, tamper dots, color codes, mini planner iconsKiss cut sheets or rolls
1"Simple logo, or 1 to 2 words at 7 ptLogo dots for packaging, lip balm tops, phone case decorationSheets, rolls or singles
1.5"Logo plus a short line, or a small QR codeBox seals, sample vial labels, giveaway minisSingles or sheets
2"Logo, product name, a line of textJar lid labels, mini product labels, laptop minisSingles, sheets or rolls

Below 0.5" the cut becomes unreliable and the sticker is hard to peel, so that is our floor. A 0.8" QR code is the smallest that scans consistently from a phone, which rules it out below the 1.5" row.

Most problems with mini stickers are in the artwork, not the printing. These are the rules we check on every proof.

  • Type size: 6 pt is the smallest that reads; 7 pt or larger for anything that matters. Avoid thin or light typefaces, which break up on the press at that size.
  • Line weight: keep strokes at 0.25 pt or heavier. Hairlines vanish, and fine outlines around a logo print as gaps.
  • Cut tolerance: the blade can drift up to 1/32". On a 1" sticker, give the art a 1/16" margin from the cut line so nothing important gets clipped.
  • Detail in die cuts: inside corners and spikes under 1/16" wide will tear on the peel. Round them or add a thin border.
  • Color: small areas of color look lighter than in the file. Boost saturation a touch, and skip gradients, which band at mini sizes.
  • Bleed: extend backgrounds 0.0625" past the cut line so a tiny white edge does not show.

Sizing a design down from a bigger sticker rarely works as a plain shrink, and our guide to custom sticker sizes covers how to simplify a logo for each size step.

sections.h2: Sheets, rolls or singles for minis
sections.html: How a small sticker is supplied matters more than it does for larger pieces, because peeling a 0.75" sticker off its own backing is slow. Kiss cut sheets hold dozens of minis on one 4" x 6" or 5" x 7" backing, which is the right format for planner stickers, mixed icon sets and anything applied by hand in a studio. Rolls are the choice for labeling at any volume: a roll of 1" seals feeds a hand dispenser or applicator and keeps the labels in order, and SKU or batch numbers can run sequentially along the roll. Singles are only worth it from about 1.5" up, for minis dropped into orders or sold in packs. Shape options at every size are grouped under the shape and size sticker categories, and all of them come down to this scale.

1. Pick the size from the table and decide what has to be on it. If it does not fit at 7 pt, go up a size rather than down a type size.
  2. Send artwork as vector (AI, EPS, SVG, PDF) wherever possible; a 300 dpi PNG or JPG at final size works for simple shapes but loses crispness on fine logos. Free design support will simplify a logo for mini use.
  3. Choose the stock: vinyl or BOPP for jars, bottles and anything that gets wet; paper or kraft for dry packaging and envelopes; clear for a label that should disappear on glass.
  4. Choose the format: sheets, rolls or singles, and the quantity. The minimum is 100 stickers, and minis are usually ordered in the thousands because they go fast.
  5. Check the free digital proof at actual size on screen or print it on a desktop printer; a mini that looks fine zoomed in can be unreadable at 1".
  6. Production takes 5 to 7 business days after approval, with free FedEx shipping in the United States.

Prices start at $0.30 per sticker and small sizes sit at the low end of the range; the rest of the materials and finishes we print are on the Die Cut Stickers home page.

faqs.q: What is the smallest custom sticker you can print?
faqs.a: 0.5" on the longest side. Below that the die cut becomes unreliable and the sticker is too small to peel by hand. At 0.5" there is room for an icon, a letter or a solid color dot, but no text; the first size that carries a word or two at 7 pt is 1".

faqs.q: Can a mini sticker carry readable text?
faqs.a: From 1" up, yes, at 7 pt or larger in a regular or bold typeface. A 1" circle holds a logo and one or two words; a 2" sticker holds a logo, a product name and a line of text. Below 1", drop the text and let the icon do the work.

faqs.q: Do custom tiny stickers come on sheets or individually?
faqs.a: Both, but sheets are the sensible choice under 1.5". A kiss cut 4" x 6" or 5" x 7" sheet holds dozens of minis and peels far faster than singles. For labeling products in volume, rolls on a 3" core keep the minis in order for a dispenser or applicator.

faqs.q: Will a QR code work on a small sticker?
faqs.a: Only from 1.5" up. A QR code needs to be at least 0.8" square with a plain margin to scan reliably from a phone, which leaves no room on a 1" sticker. On a 1.5" or 2" sticker it fits beside a logo, and we show it at actual size on the proof so you can test it.

faqs.q: How accurate is the die cut on a 1 inch sticker?
faqs.a: The blade can drift up to 1/32" from the cut line, which is invisible on a large sticker but noticeable on a mini. Keep important art 1/16" inside the cut line and extend backgrounds 1/16" past it, and any drift falls in the bleed rather than through your logo.

faqs.q: Can small stickers be die cut to a logo shape rather than a circle?
faqs.a: Yes, down to about 0.75". Keep the outline simple: inside corners and points narrower than 1/16" tear on the peel, so we may add a thin border around a detailed logo. Circles and rounded squares peel best under 0.75" and are what we suggest for seals and dots.

faqs.q: What material should mini stickers be for jar lids and lip balm tubes?
faqs.a: Vinyl or BOPP with a laminate, since both get handled, wiped and sometimes wet. Clear BOPP gives a printed-on look on a glass jar lid. Paper and kraft are for dry uses only: envelope seals, bakery boxes and tags, where cost matters more than water resistance.

faqs.q: How many custom miniature stickers do I need to order?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 stickers, but minis are usually ordered by the thousand because a sheet or roll goes through them quickly. Prices start at $0.30 per sticker and small sizes sit at the cheap end, with the per-sticker cost falling steeply on sheets and rolls.

faqs.q: Why does my logo look blurry when I shrink it to 1 inch?
faqs.a: Usually because the file is a raster image sized for a larger sticker, or because the logo has fine lines and small text that cannot survive the scale. Send a vector file (AI, EPS, SVG or PDF) and simplify the mark: thicken strokes, drop the tagline and keep the main shape.

faqs.q: Can you print planner and journal stickers as mixed sheets?
faqs.a: Yes. A kiss cut sheet can carry many different icons, labels and shapes in one layout, each peeling off separately while the backing stays whole. Matte paper or matte vinyl both take pen and pencil, so planner users can write on the stickers after applying them.

faqs.q: Will a small sticker stay on a curved surface like a vial or a pen?
faqs.a: Yes, if the sticker is narrow in the direction of the curve. A 0.5" x 1.5" rectangle wraps a sample vial cleanly, while a 1.5" circle on the same vial lifts at the edges. Vinyl flexes better than paper on tight curves, and permanent adhesive holds best.

faqs.q: Can I check a mini sticker before the whole run is printed?
faqs.a: The free digital proof is sized so you can view it at actual size on screen or print it on a desktop printer, which catches almost every legibility problem before production. Compare a 1" print of the proof against a coin to judge the real type size.
